items.headline: Brandon Aiyuk (ACL + MCL) listed as out
items.news: Aiyuk's effort to secure his release by reporting to the 49ers' facility Friday could be complicated by roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture he owes the team, Tom Pelissero of NFL Network reports.
items.analysis: Pelissero notes that the NFL Management Council and the NFL Players Association are both involved in trying to reaching a resolution that is agreeable to both Aiyuk and the 49ers. It's possible that the embattled wideout could ultimately agree to pay back the money in order to potentially have an opportunity to move on with another club, but there's also a chance the issue goes to arbitration. Aiyuk is planning to show up at San Francisco's facility Friday, though that is unlikely to bring the matter to a close. In fact, it could take an extended period of time to sort out a path forward, especially if arbitration is brought into play.

items.headline: Garrett Wilson (concussion) listed as questionable
items.news: Wilson (concussion) did not practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Wilson remains in concussion protocol and has not practiced thus far this week. He was placed in protocol midweek, which makes it an uphill climb for him to be cleared for Sunday's game at the Chiefs. If Wilson can't clear protocol, fantasy managers can expect more targets for Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper.

items.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) listed as questionable
items.news: Henderson (illness) was listed as a non-participant in Thursday's practice, ESPN's Rob Demovsky reports.
items.analysis: Henderson officially goes down as a non-participant for a second consecutive Week 9 practice and has now missed a full week due to this illness. His participation level will be worth monitoring Friday, though it looks likely at this point that Henderson will carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Packers. Corey Kiner would be in line to maintain an expanded role alongside Rhamondre Stevenson if Henderson sits again Sunday.

items.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle) listed as questionable
items.news: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer hopes that Ferguson (ankle) will be "back on the field" Friday, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
items.analysis: Ferguson did not get any work in Wednesday or Thursday due to the ankle injury he sustained in Week 8, but it appears there is a chance he could practice in some capacity Friday. The Cowboys will reveal his official status for Week 9 at some point following the conclusion of Friday's session.

items.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Pickens (hamstring) "will be a little bit limited" Friday, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer is "hopeful" he will play Sunday against the Colts, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
items.analysis: Pickens was limited at practice both Wednesday and Thursday due to a hamstring issue, and it appears he will find himself in a similar spot at Friday's practice. The Cowboys will provide another update on his status after the latest session comes to a close.

items.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: "It does not seem" that Skattebo (hamstring) will play Sunday against the Eagles, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.analysis: A hamstring injury sustained prior to the Giants' Week 8 bye prevented Skattebo from practicing both Wednesday and Thursday, and although he will have one more chance to get some work in before game designations are determined, it appears the injury will keep him off the field for Week 9.

items.headline: Breece Hall (quadriceps) injury update
items.news: Hall (quadriceps) "has been medically cleared" and is expected to play Sunday against the Chiefs, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.analysis: Hall has not taken the field since sustaining a quad injury in Week 3, but he practiced fully Thursday and appears primed to return to action Sunday. Braelon Allen has shined in Hall's absence, but Hall entered the season as the starter, so both figure to be involved to some degree in Week 9.

items.headline: Deshaun Watson (concussion) listed as questionable
items.news: Watson (concussion) "is unlikely to start" Sunday's game against the Saints, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.analysis: Watson has not practiced since being placed in the NFL's concussion protocol Tuesday, and it appears he will not be cleared to suit up for Week 9. The Browns will provide an official update on Watson's status later Friday, and if he is unable to go, Shedeur Sanders would presumably get the start in his place.

items.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) ruled out
items.news: Robinson (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bengals, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
items.analysis: Though Robinson was able to practice in a limited capacity Wednesday through Friday and was initially deemed questionable for Week 9, he was downgraded shortly thereafter and will not be available for Sunday's game in Madrid. In Robinson's continued absence, look for Khalil Herbert to be elevated from the practice squad to work in a complementary role behind Bijan Robinson.

items.headline: Michael Wilson (rest/ribs) listed as questionable
items.news: Wilson (rest/ribs) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
items.analysis: Wilson continues to don a yellow non-contact jersey on the practice field as he deals with two broken ribs, so his activity level comes as no surprise. Friday's injury report will determine if Wilson enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Seattle, but he's already demonstrated an ability to play through the issue, notching a 79 percent snap share, reeling in eight of 15 targets for 111 yards and one touchdown and recording a 17-yard carry in this past Sunday's win in Dallas.

items.headline: Matthew Stafford (right elbow) practice update
items.news: Stafford (right elbow) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN reports.
items.analysis: Stafford was seen leaving the locker room with his upper right arm wrapped in ice after this past Sunday's win against the Chargers. Head coach Sean McVay told Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register on Monday that Stafford has been tending to arm soreness, but the quarterback clarified the situation with Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times on Wednesday, stating that he's had his right arm wrapped in ice regularly this season. An uncapped session to begin Week 9 prep puts Stafford in the clear to continue to lead the Ram's offense Sunday in Washington.

items.headline: Alvin Kamara (rest/back) listed as questionable
items.news: Kamara (rest/back) returned to practice Thursday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
items.analysis: The veteran RB was back on the field Thursday after getting a rest day to open the practice week. Kamara has also dealt with a back issue that limited his practice participation in recent weeks. The Saints are coming off a bye, so the added time off likely bodes well for Kamara being closer to full strength heading into Week 9 against the Browns. New Orleans' practice report will provide insight on Kamara's participation level, but he seems to be trending in the right direction regardless.

items.headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) remains on IR
items.news: Tyson (hamstring) remained a limited participant at Thursday's practice, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Tyson has logged consecutive limited practices since having his 21-day window to return from IR opened Wednesday. The rookie first-round pick could make his NFL regular-season debut as soon as Sunday against the Browns, though the Saints may want him to log at least one full practice before seeing game action. For his part, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football suggested that from his point of view Tyson didn't look limited Thursday. In any case, the wideout's return to action, be it this week or next, would be proceeded by an official move adding him to the 53-man roster.

items.headline: Drew Lock (right elbow) listed as questionable
items.news: Lock (right elbow) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
items.analysis: Lock is poised to fill in for Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) this Sunday against the Cardinals, but the former still has some work to do to avoid a designation for that contest after a second straight capped session to begin Week 9 prep. Friday's injury report will reveal if Lock's right elbow issue is behind him, though he appears close to being healthy, as he told Brady Henderson of ESPN.com on Thursday that it's "doing a lot better... (It) felt great to get under center, rip some balls yesterday."

items.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Shaheed (knee) didn't participate at the Seahawks' practice Thursday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
items.analysis: Shaheed has now missed back-to-back practices to open the week as he continues to work his way back from the knee injury that forced him to miss the team's Week 8 loss to Chicago. The wide receiver's chances to play Sunday versus Arizona seem thin, so Tory Horton could serve as the team's No. 3 option at wide receiver again in Week 9.

items.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) listed as questionable
items.news: Burks (foot) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Burks is mimicking his practice regimen from a week ago, when he kicked it off with back-to-back DNPs due to a foot issue. If he follows last week's regimen, he'll be limited Friday and enter the weekend listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Rams. While playing through the injury this past Sunday against the Eagles, he tallied a 68 percent snap share and recorded three catches (on five targets) for 81 yards.

items.headline: David Njoku (fibula) remains on IR
items.news: Njoku (fibula) was limited in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Njoku had his 21-day practice window opener Wednesday, and he's logged back-to-back limited practice sessions to begin Week 9 work. He's been on the shelf since going down with the lower leg injury in Week 2.

items.headline: James Conner (foot) remains on IR
items.news: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Tuesday that Conner (foot) won't return from IR this week, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports.
items.analysis: Though LaFleur said last week that Conner could "potentially" play this season, that won't happen in Week 9. The veteran running back continues to work his way back from a right foot injury and has not yet been cleared to practice. Arizona is dealing with multiple injuries in its backfield, including Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion), so Conner could provide a big boost once he's able to work his way back this week. Instead, the team will turn to Tyler Allgeier to lead its backfield, with Evan Hull serving as his primary backup if Knight is unable to suit up Sunday against Seattle.

items.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) injury update
items.news: Tuten (ankle/foot) rushed 12 times for 29 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night.
items.analysis: Tuten fought through the pair of lower-body injuries that made him a game-time decision, recording his fourth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a one-yard run to cap off the opening possession of the contest. The second-year back had to grind for every yard he got on the ground, but fortunately for Tuten, the Jaguars built a comfortable enough lead where he was able to benefit from an early end to his night. Tuten has now scored in back-to-back games, and he'll have some extra time to get healthier ahead of a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

items.headline: Dalton Kincaid (chest) listed as questionable
items.news: Kincaid (chest) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice,.
items.analysis: Fellow pass catchers DJ Moore (shoulder) and Keon Coleman (shoulder) also were limited Thursday, so the trio's statuses will need to be monitored ahead of Monday night's game against the Vikings. Over his last two outings, Kincaid has managed to make his mark from a fantasy perspective by logging an 11-124-1 receiving line in that span.

items.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) listed as questionable
items.news: St. Brown (ribs) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports.
items.analysis: St. Brown maintained his activity level from Wednesday's walkthrough as he navigates a rib injury, which was likely the reason for his brief time on the sideline this past Sunday against the Vikings. He thus has one more chance to get back to full Friday, or else he'll be at risk of entering the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Miami.

items.headline: Malik Nabers (undisclosed) listed as questionable
items.news: Nabers (undisclosed) said Thursday, "I'll be good," for Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Art Stapleton of USA Today reports.
items.analysis: Nabers was spotted working with the Giants' training staff during the media-access portion of Thursday's practice, one day removed from not being on the team's initial Week 9 injury report. The reason for his likely practice restrictions isn't known but will be revealed once New York posts its second injury report of the week.

items.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) injury update
items.news: Rice (hamstring/knee) practiced without limitations Thursday.
items.analysis: Rice is off the injury report Thursday after kicking off Week 9 prep with a limited session Wednesday. The oft-injured wide receiver has been limited to five appearances this season, one of which he left before recording a catch, but he has 20 catches for 243 yards and two touchdowns across the other four games. With Rice getting healthier, he could feast Sunday against a Jets defense that's allowing 30.7 points per game during an active three-game losing streak.

items.headline: Lamar Jackson (thumb) placed on IR
items.news: The Ravens have officially placed Jackson (thumb) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: Prior to Thursday night's game against the Jaguars, the Ravens made a trio of moves to re-shape their Week 9 QB corps. Along with Jackson, Tyler Huntley (toe) landed on IR, while Austin Reed was added to the team's active roster. As a result, Joe Fagnano (Thursday's starter), Kedon Slovis and Austin Reed are available to face Jacksonville, and then in the coming days Jacoby Brissett will be on his way to Baltimore via a looming trade with the Cardinals. Jackson will miss his team's next four games, at a minimum, and it's possible that his injury could be season ending, an outcome that is already reportedly in the cards for Huntley.

items.headline: Dyami Brown (calf) listed as questionable
items.news: Brown (calf) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Brown was a full practice participant Wednesday but was downgraded to limited Thursday. The 27-year-old is now seemingly in danger of missing the Week 9 meeting with the Rams. However, since Brown hasn't been very involved throughout the 2026 campaign, his absence wouldn't open up many opportunities for others.

items.headline: Nikko Remigio (hip) practice update
items.news: Remigio (hip) was a full participant at the Chiefs' practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Remigio opened the week with a limited practice Wednesday as a result of a hip injury, but he now appears to be good to go for Week 9. The wide receiver will operate in his role as the team's primary kickoff and punt returner versus the Jets on Sunday.

items.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) listed as questionable
items.news: Parkinson (ribs) remained sidelined for Thursday's practice, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
items.analysis: Parkinson hasn't practiced since being injured in Week 7, and he looks headed for a possible second straight absence. With Terrance Ferguson (ankle) looking like he has a chance to return from injured reserve Sunday against the Commanders, it could be Ferguson, Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen handling tight-end duties.

items.headline: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) nearing return from IR
items.news: Ferguson (ankle) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
items.analysis: Ferguson has been sidelined since spraining his ankle in Week 3 at Denver, missing the last five games a result. The Rams designated him for return from injured reserve Wednesday, and he's managed two limited sessions since then. Friday's practice report will determine if Ferguson has a chance to return to action Sunday in Washington, but he'll still need to be activated from IR by Saturday afternoon to be in a position to do so.

items.headline: Zonovan Knight (concussion) listed as questionable
items.news: Knight (concussion) officially didn't practice Thursday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
items.analysis: Since exiting Week 8 action with a concussion, Knight hasn't been able to log any practice reps, which generally isn't a good sign that he'll be available Sunday at Seattle. Arizona may make a ruling on Knight's status once it posts Friday's injury report, and if he's indeed sidelined for that contest, Tyler Allgeier stands to serve as the team's workhorse running back this weekend, with Evan Hull likely backing him up.

items.headline: Jake Elliott (ankle) listed as questionable
items.news: Elliott (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Elliott was limited for a second consecutive practice. There should be more clarity on his status Friday for the Eagles' Week 9 meeting with the Giants. However, if Elliott is ruled out ahead of that one, the Eagles will presumably hit the open market for a replacement.

items.headline: Dont'e Thornton Jr. (back) listed as questionable
items.news: Thornton (back) was a limited participant at the Raiders' practice Thursday, Paul Gutierrez of the team's official site reports.
items.analysis: Thornton was added to the injury report with an apparent back injury after opening the week as a full participant Wednesday. The fact that the wide receiver was able to practice in any capacity is a positive sign, but he will have one more chance to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with the 49ers.

items.headline: Tanner McKee (rib) listed as questionable
items.news: McKee (rib) was limited in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: McKee recently lost the starting quarterback job to Joe Milton. As if things couldn't get any worse, the signal-caller appears to be in danger of missing the NFC East showdown with the Giants. If McKee can't suit up for that contest, 2026 fifth-round pick Cole Payton would presumably back up Milton against New York in Week 9.

items.headline: Christian Kirk (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Kirk (knee) didn't practice Thursday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: Kirk kicked off Week 9 prep with a limited session Wednesday due to a knee injury, so his downgrade one day later may be cause for concern. Friday's practice report could provide some clarity surrounding his status ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.

items.headline: Demarcus Robinson (ankle) nearing return from IR
items.news: Robinson (ankle) practiced on a limited basis Thursday.
items.analysis: Since the 49ers designated him for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Robinson has logged back-to-back capped sessions. GM John Lynch said Thursday on KNBR radio that the 49ers expect Robinson to be available Sunday against the Raiders, which can't be said for fellow WRs Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), per Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area. Friday's injury report will reveal Robinson's odds to return this weekend, but he'll still need to be activated by Saturday afternoon to have a chance to do so.

items.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) listed as questionable
items.news: Jennings (calf) was limited in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: It's a new injury for Jennings, but he has an extra day to recover this week, as the Vikings play the Bills on Monday night. Jennings has six grabs for 54 yards on 10 targets across six games this season and is nowhere near fantasy relevance in his current role.

items.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) listed as questionable
items.news: Wicks (ankle) did not practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Wicks appears headed for a third straight absence Sunday against the Giants. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also continues to miss practice time. It could again be Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore at receiver for the Eagles in Week 9.

items.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Smith (hamstring) officially didn't practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Smith has yet to mix into any drills since his last appearance in Week 6 against the Panthers, missing the last two contests due to a hamstring issue. With a Week 10 bye on the horizon, the Eagles may be focusing on getting him healthy for the final eight weeks of the campaign. In any case, Smith's status for Sunday's contest against the Giants may gain some clarity once the team posts its final Week 9 injury report Friday.

items.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) practice update
items.news: Kelce (ankle) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
items.analysis: Kelce was deemed a limited participant Wednesday, but the tight end's full participation Thursday paves the way for him to be in uniform Sunday against the Jets. Over his last two games, the Chiefs' leader in catches and receiving yards has amassed nine catches (on 15 targets) for 111 yards with a TD, and as long as he stays healthy he'll merit weekly fantasy lineup consideration.

items.headline: Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Samuel (hamstring) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: Prior to the 49ers' Week 8 bye, head coach Kyle Shanahan expressed optimism that Samuel may be able to return in Week 9, but the tide turned Thursday, when GM told KNBR radio that the wide receiver isn't likely to play Sunday against the Raiders, according to Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area. With two DNPs under his belt so far and one more chance to practice Friday, Samuel appears to be in line for his third missed game in a row due to a right hamstring injury.

items.headline: Mike Evans (achilles) listed as questionable
items.news: Evans (Achilles) didn't participate in Thursday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: After back-to-back DNPs to open Week 9 prep, Evans technically has one more chance to mix into drills this week, but GM John Lynch said on KNBR radio Thursday that the wide receiver likely won't be available Sunday versus the Raiders due to his lingering right Achilles issue, per Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area. The 49ers may make a ruling on Evans' status as soon as they post Friday's injury report.

items.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: McCaffrey (hamstring) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: McCaffrey followed up Wednesday's lack of activity with some on-field work one day later, but he may need to practice fully Friday in order to avoid a designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders. He's tending to a left hamstring injury from a Week 7 loss in Atlanta, when he managed just a 52 percent snap share and churned out 100 yards from scrimmage and a rushing TD on 13 touches.

items.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) listed as questionable
items.news: Barkley (hamstring/back) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
items.analysis: Barkley followed up Wednesday's DNP with some activity one day later as he deals with lingering hamstring and back injuries. Friday's practice report will determine if he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game against the Giants. While playing through those health concerns this past Sunday in Washington, Barkley logged a 32 percent snap share and racked up 14 touches for 54 yards from scrimmage and one rushing TD.

items.headline: Ty Johnson (illness) listed as questionable
items.news: Johnson (illness) did not practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Johnson will have an extra day to rest up this week, as the Bills host the Vikings on Monday night. Buffalo's preferred pass-catching back, Johnson has rushed six times for just 10 yards through six games this season, but he has caught all 15 of his targets for 174 yards.

items.headline: Keon Coleman (shoulder) listed as questionable
items.news: Coleman (shoulder) was limited in practice Thursday.
items.analysis: It's a new injury for Coleman, who is on the injury report for the first time since Week 4. With both DJ Moore (knee) and Dalton Kincaid (chest) healthy last Sunday against the Ravens, Coleman caught just one pass for four yards on three targets.

items.headline: Joshua Palmer (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Palmer (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
items.analysis: The veteran wideout was injured in Sunday's win over the Ravens and was unable to return to the contest. If he's unable to play Monday night against the Vikings, Skyler Bell and Greg Dortch could see additional work on offense.

items.headline: DJ Moore (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Moore (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Moore mustered some level of activity in Buffalo's first practice of Week 9 after downplaying the knee injury that forced him out late in the Week 8 win over Baltimore. He has an extra day to recover before the Bills face the Vikings on Monday Night Football. Moore has two more chances to practice without limitations and put himself in the clear to suit up.

items.headline: Jaylen Wright (quadriceps) listed as questionable
items.news: Wright (quadriceps) was limited in Thursday's practice, Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Wright has been battling various issues all season and hasn't been effective when on the field, yet he's still operating as the Dolphins' lightly-used RB2 behind Ollie Gordon. Wright is averaging a microscopic 1.9 yards per carry this season.

items.headline: MarShawn Lloyd (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Lloyd was limited at practice Thursday due to a knee injury.
items.analysis: Lloyd's addition to the Packers' practice report midweek is something to monitor, especially because it may indicate a health concern that occurred during Thursday's session. Ultimately, Friday's injury report may provide some clarity into the situation.

items.headline: Tyler Huntley (toe) placed on IR
items.news: Huntley (toe) was placed on injured reserve Thursday.
items.analysis: Huntley and Lamar Jackson (thumb) were both placed on injured reserve Thursday. The latter still has at least a slim chance to return this season, while Huntley's injury has been confirmed to be season-ending. Joe Fagnano is set to start Thursday's game against the Jaguars before reinforcements arrive under center in the form of Jacoby Brissett, for whom the Ravens are expected to finalize a trade over the weekend.

items.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) listed as questionable
items.news: Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) did not practice Thursday, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: After being limited Wednesday, Donaldson's downgrade to DNP puts him in jeopardy of missing Week 9 against the Browns. With Travis Etienne (hamstring) also looking unlikely to play, the Saints could be rolling with Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller and Audric Estime out of the backfield.

items.headline: Drew Ogletree (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Ogletree (knee) upgraded to a limited practice Thursday.
items.analysis: After being a DNP on Wednesday, Ogletree's return to practice puts him on track for Sunday's game against Dallas. The Colts are using four tight ends most weeks, featuring Tyler Warren in the passing game, while Mo Alie-Cox, Ogletree and Will Mallory play part-time roles.

items.headline: Harold Fannin Jr. (groin) listed as questionable
items.news: Fannin (groin) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
items.analysis: Fannin wasn't listed on Wednesday's injury report, so his appearance on it a day later is notable. It remains to be seen if Thursday's listed limitations were maintenance related or indicative of a setback, but the tight end may need to work fully Friday in order to approach Sunday's game against the Saints without an injury designation.

items.headline: Christian Watson (ribs) listed as questionable
items.news: Watson (ribs) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Watson now has back-to-back capped sessions under his belt to begin Week 9 prep, which stems from the broken rib that he suffered during last Thursday's win against the Panthers. He'll have one more chance Friday to get back to full participation, at which point the Packers may tag him with a designation for Sunday's contest at New England.

items.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Brown (ankle/knee) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Thursday's injury report confirms Brown's absence after he wasn't spotted earlier in the day. Brown has missed the team's first two practices leading up to Sunday's game against the Packers, suggesting he's fighting an uphill battle in his effort to avoid missing a second consecutive game. He has dressed for only three of New England's first eight games. DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, Kyle Williams and possibly Mack Hollins (calf) would lead the Patriots' wide receiver room Sunday if Brown sits again.

items.headline: Denzel Boston (calf) listed as questionable
items.news: Boston (calf) remained limited in Thursday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
items.analysis: Boston dealt with a foot issue a couple weeks ago, but the calf injury is new this week. The rookie wideout has been scuffling after a hot start to the season. Perhaps the likely insertion of Shedeur Sanders this Sunday against the Saints can help Boston regain his big-play ability. Boston is a low-floor, upside WR4 for fantasy.

items.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) listed as questionable
items.news: Henry (foot) wasn't spotted at Thursday's practice, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
items.analysis: Henry has started Week 9 prep with back-to-back absences after exiting during the Patriots' Week 8 win over Miami. If the veteran tight end is unable to practice in at least some capacity Friday, he'll likely be ruled out for Sunday's game against the Packers, paving the way for rookie third-round pick Eli Raridon to take on an expanded role.

items.headline: Zavier Scott (wrist) placed on IR
items.news: The Bears placed Scott (wrist) on injured reserve Thursday.
items.analysis: Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games. He's appeared in four contests this season, playing 65 snaps on special teams.

items.headline: Mason Taylor (back) practice update
items.news: Taylor (back) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Taylor was limited Wednesday, but his return to full Thursday puts him on track for his normal role Sunday against the Chiefs. The tight end has been a surprisingly big part of the passing offense this season despite the selection of Kenyon Sadiq in the first round of April's Draft. Taylor has secured 17 of 23 targets for 136 yards and two touchdowns across six games.

items.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) practice update
items.news: Egbuka (foot) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
items.analysis: After missing Wednesday's practice, Egbuka was back in the mix in full on Thursday. The second-year wideout has missed the last two games due to a concussion and a foot injury, but appears to be on track to return Sunday in Chicago. Getting Egbuka back in the fold would be a boon for a Buccaneers' passing game which has yet to hit its stride this season.

items.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) listed as questionable
items.news: Monangai (thumb/toe) didn't practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Monangai also missed Wednesday's walkthrough due to the turf-toe injury that has sidelined him the last four contests. With no activity to speak of so far and just one more chance to practice this week, he seems to be trending toward another absence Sunday against the Buccaneers, something that may be confirmed on Friday's injury report. D'Andre Swift will continue to pace the Bears backfield for as long as Monangai is sidelined, with Roschon Johnson on hand for any RB reps that linger.

items.headline: Kenny Gainwell (hip) practice update
items.news: Gainwell (hip) was a full practice participant Thursday, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
items.analysis: Gainwell also tended to a hip injury last week, when he got back to full by Friday, but he still entered the weekend listed as questionable for Week 8 action. He proceeded to suit up this past Sunday against the Falcons and split Tampa Bay's backfield with Bucky Irving, logging a 50 percent snap share and going for 140 yards on 25 carries in rainy conditions. Considering Gainwell followed up Wednesday's limited session with an uncapped one Thursday, he's good to go for Sunday's road showdown with the Bears.

items.headline: Beaux Collins (hip) remains on IR
items.news: Collins (hip) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, D. Orlando Ledbetter of BowTieSports.com reports.
items.analysis: Collins remains on injured reserve but had his 21-day practice window opened two weeks ago. He's yet to play in a game this season.

items.headline: Britain Covey (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Covey is listed as questionable with a knee injury.

items.headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Murray likely won't play Monday against the Bills due to a hamstring strain, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: Per head coach Kevin O'Connell, Murray is considered week-to-week, paving the way for Carson Wentz to make his second start of the season when the Vikings face the Bills on MNF. Per Lewis, O'Connell said Thursday that a stint on injured reserve isn't under consideration for Murray, suggesting that the starting quarterback's potential absence isn't expected to linger beyond 1-to-3 weeks.

items.headline: Jalen McMillan (knee) remains on IR
items.news: McMillan (knee) isn't expected back until after Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
items.analysis: McMillan was initially given a return timetable of 6-to-8 weeks after aggravating a PCL sprain in his left knee in Week 3. Head coach Todd Bowles said McMillan won't have his window to return from IR opened before the Buccaneers face the Bears on Sunday, and Tampa Bay will be on bye the following week, so McMillan's next chance to play won't come until Nov. 22 at Detroit.

items.headline: Sam Darnold (quadriceps) ruled out
items.news: Darnold (quadriceps), who has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, is considered week-to-week, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Head coach Mike Macdonald labeled Darnold week-to-week Wednesday while adding that Darnold isn't expected to be placed on injured reserve due to his injury. Backup Drew Lock missed the previous two games due to an elbow injury but has a chance to return Sunday against the Cardinals and take over the starting role. If Lock isn't ready to suit up, 2025 third-round pick Jalen Milroe could be tabbed for the first regular-season start of the latter's NFL career. Per Henderson, Macdonald also revealed that Darnold suffered a cracked rib on the second play of Seattle's Week 8 loss to the Bears, but the QB managed to play through that injury and eventually injured his quadriceps late in the game.

items.headline: Jalen Hurts (calf) remains on IR
items.news: Hurts is on injured reserve with a calf injury.

items.headline: Alec Pierce (heel) nearing return from IR
items.news: When asked Wednesday when Pierce (heel) might be able to return to practice, Colts head coach Shane Steichen noted that he "can't put a timetable on it right now," Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan Indianapolis reports.
items.analysis: Steichen said that Pierce, who has been on IR since Sept. 26, is currently rehabbing his injury, but the wideout's return is clearly not imminent. At 2-6, the Colts, who are already sellers ahead of the NFL trade deadline, have little incentive to rush Pierce back. Meanwhile, fellow WR Josh Downs has asked to be dealt, a situation that further clouds the team's pass-catching corps ahead of Week 9.

items.headline: Jordan Whittington (back) listed as questionable
items.news: Whittington (back) was a limited participant at the Rams' practice Wednesday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Whittington was questionable to play in Week 8 versus the Chargers due to a back injury, but he was able to give it a go, failing to catch his only target while securing one tackle on special teams in the contest. The wide receiver will have two more chances to log a full practice before Sunday's contest against the Commanders.

items.headline: Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Jones Jr. is listed as questionable with a hamstring injury.

items.headline: Chris Brooks (ankle) nearing return from IR
items.news: Brooks (ankle) was designated to return from injured reserve by the Packers on Wednesday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.analysis: Brooks was a limited participant at the team's first practice of the week as Green Bay opened his 21-day practice window Wednesday. The running back has been on IR since suffering an ankle injury in Week 4 against the Buccaneers, but he could be nearing a return to action.

items.headline: Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) nearing return from IR
items.news: Head coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that the Saints haven't opened Etienne's (hamstring) practice window just yet, Jeff Nowak of WWL Louisiana reports.
items.analysis: Etienne has missed the required four games on IR due to a strained left hamstring, but even with the benefit of a Week 8 bye, he hasn't gained clearance to mix into drills. Moore told Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana on Monday that Etienne has a chance to return to practice this week, but with no on-field work to begin Week 9 prep, he seems to be on the outside looking in to have enough time to be activated for Sunday's contest against the Browns.

items.headline: Ronnie Rivers (calf) nearing return from IR
items.news: Rivers (calf) was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
items.analysis: Rivers made his return to practice Wednesday, operating as a full participant at the team's first session of the week, per Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports. The running back has been on injured reserve since late September after suffering a calf injury in Week 2 against the Giants, but he could be back in action as soon as Sunday versus the Commanders.

items.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) listed as questionable
items.news: Turpin (ribs) did not practice Wednesday, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.
items.analysis: Turpin has missed the past two contests with the injury, and his Week 9 prep isn't off on the right foot. Jonathan Mingo and Camden Brown handled reserve wideout duties behind CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens (hamstring) and Ryan Flournoy last Sunday against the Cardinals.

items.headline: Kaytron Allen (quadriceps) listed as questionable
items.news: Allen (quadriceps) was a limited participant at the Dolphins' practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Allen played 16 snaps on special teams in Miami's 24-19 loss to the Patriots in Week 8, and he may have picked up a quadriceps injury in the process. The running back will have two more chances to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with Detroit.

items.headline: Will Kacmarek (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Kacmarek (hamstring) was a limited participant at the Dolphins' practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Kacmarek was limited at practice throughout the entire week before playing 19 offensive snaps and six snaps on special teams during the team's 24-19 loss to the Patriots in Week 8. The tight end may be set for a similar fate ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Lions as he continues to nurse a hamstring injury.

items.headline: Theo Johnson (neck) practice update
items.news: Johnson (neck) was a full participant at the Giants' practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.analysis: Johnson appears to be back to full health after missing the team's last two contests while nursing a neck injury. The 25-year-old will be back in his No. 2 role at tight end behind starter Isaiah Likely against the Eagles on Sunday.

items.headline: Adam Randall (neck) nearing return from IR
items.news: Randall (neck) is officially listed as questionable for Thursday's game versus the Jaguars, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports.
items.analysis: Randall was not considered to be limited during Baltimore's walkthrough practice Wednesday but he's still on IR going into game-day. If he's not activated for Week 9, his next opportunity to make his regular-season debut would come in Week 10 versus the Chargers.

items.headline: Pat Bryant (ankle) remains on IR
items.news: Bryant (ankle) was a full participant at the Broncos' practice Wednesday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
items.analysis: After being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Bryant was back on the practice field with no restrictions. With a bye looming for the Broncos in Week 10, it's unclear if the team will decide to activate the wide receiver before Sunday's matchup with the Panthers. Regardless of whatever decision the team makes, Bryant appears to be fully recovered from the ankle injury that has sidelined him since Week 4.

items.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) nearing return from IR
items.news: The Patriots are expected to designate Hollins (calf) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.analysis: Hollins' last game appearance came back in Week 4, but with his return to practice on the horizon, he could be an option for the Patriots as soon as this Sunday's game against the Packers. With Romeo Doubs (shoulder) currently on IR and A.J. Brown's (ankle/knee) availability for Week 9 looking cloudy, Hollins could have a chance at claiming a meaningful role right off the bat if he's cleared to play versus Green Bay. Prior to sustaining the calf injury, Hollins logged a 15-209-0 receiving line on 20 targets through New England's first four games.

items.headline: David Montgomery (groin) ruled out
items.news: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday that Montgomery (groin) has made some progress but is still viewed as week-to-week and will remain out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
items.analysis: Montgomery missed Houston's last two games before a Week 8 bye, and he doesn't look like he'll be ready to return to action any sooner than Nov. 15, when the Texans face the Browns on the road. With Montgomery set to miss another game, Woody Marks is poised to maintain a lead role out of the backfield. While Montgomery was sidelined the previous two contests, Marks averaged 81.0 scrimmage yards on 18.5 touches per game.

items.headline: Jacob Saylors (neck) listed as questionable
items.news: Saylors (neck) is not expected to practice Wednesday, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
items.analysis: Saylor's neck injury is significant enough that Coach Dan Campbell felt comfortable declaring him doubtful to practice multiple days in advance. The kick returner/reserve running back couldn't return to Sunday's win over the Vikings because of the injury, and it remains unclear how long he will miss.

items.headline: Jeremy McNichols (foot) placed on IR
items.news: McNichols, who suffered a foot injury Sunday against the Eagles that may require surgery, is out for the season, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.analysis: McNichols was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, and what coach Dan Quinn described as a "serious mid-foot injury" will keep the running back sidelined for the rest of the 2026 campaign. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) slated to miss at least two more games, the Commanders' current healthy RBs are Rachaad White, Austin Ekeler and Robert Henry.

items.headline: Dean Connors (hand) placed on IR
items.news: Connors (hand) was placed on IR on Tuesday, Blaine Grisak of SI.com reports.
items.analysis: Connors broke his hand in Sunday's win over the Chargers and is slated for surgery. He's worked as a core special-teamer this season but hasn't logged a snap on offense. As such, Connors' IR stint -- which will last at least four games -- isn't likely to cause any waves in fantasy.

items.headline: Kenny Yeboah placed on IR
items.news: The Cardinals placed Yeboah (undisclosed) on the practice squad injured list Tuesday.
items.analysis: Yeboah reverted to Arizona's practice squad Monday after logging no offensive snaps and just 20 snaps on special teams. The 28-year-old is unavailable for at least the next four games after being placed on the practice squad IR. Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins still lead the way at tight end.

items.headline: Tyler Loop (groin) placed on IR
items.news: The Ravens placed Loop (groin) on injured reserve Tuesday.
items.analysis: Loop emerged from Sunday's blowout loss to the Bills with a right groin injury, which will keep him out for at least the next four games. Baltimore plans to elevate or sign Jake Moody off its practice squad to take over as its kicker beginning with Thursday's game against Jacksonville. Through Baltimore's first eight contests, Loop went a perfect 18-for-18 on point-after attempts but missed four of his 17 field-goal tries.

items.headline: Kendrick Bourne (tibia) placed on IR
items.news: Arizona placed Bourne (tibia) on injured reserve Tuesday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
items.analysis: Though Bourne is expected to avoid surgery after fracturing his right tibia during Sunday's 33-30 overtime win over the Cowboys, he's facing an expected recovery timeline of three months that effectively ends his season. With Bourne heading to IR, the Cardinals signed Harrison Wallace off their practice squad to replenish their depth at receiver. The 31-year-old Bourne will finish the 2026 campaign with 26 receptions for 263 yards and no touchdowns on 38 targets over eight appearances.

items.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) placed on IR
items.news: Arizona placed Love (ankle) on injured reserve Tuesday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
items.analysis: Love's move to IR was fully expected, after Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported earlier Tuesday that the rookie first-round pick was diagnosed with a right high-ankle sprain and was facing a projected recovery timeline of 4-to-5 weeks. While Love is on the mend, Tyler Allgeier is expected to step into a lead role out of the Arizona backfield beginning with the team's Week 9 game against Seattle.

items.headline: Jonathon Brooks (core) nearing return from IR
items.news: Brooks (core) was seen working off to the side during the Panthers' unofficial practice Tuesday, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: The Panthers haven't yet opened Brooks' 21-day practice window, but that might happen soon after head coach Dave Canales said Monday that the young running back would "potentially" be designated for return from injured reserve this week. Brooks hasn't played since Week 2 after undergoing core-muscle surgery, so he'll likely need to turn in multiple full practices before the Panthers are comfortable clearing him for game action. Once he's activated from IR, Brooks will likely handle a supporting role out of the backfield behind starter Chubba Hubbard.

items.headline: Courtland Sutton (undisclosed) injury update
items.news: Sutton (undisclosed) briefly left Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
items.analysis: Sutton went to the medical tent after taking a hard hit, but the wideout was able to return to action not long after he did so. In the process he'll bolster a Denver Week 9 WR corps that also includes Jaylen Waddle, Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims and Lil'Jordan Humphrey.

items.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) injury update
items.news: Charbonnet (knee) rushed six times for 23 yards and brought in three of four targets for six yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night.
items.analysis: Charbonnet took the first carry of the night for Seattle, gaining an encouraging five yards on his first tote since tearing his left ACL in a divisional-round win over the 49ers in January. He also subsequently rattled off a 13-yard gain in the third quarter, but he was limited on his other touches and ultimately had four fewer rush attempts than Jadarian Price. Charbonnet's snap share and touches should gradually increase, and a Week 9 home matchup against the Cardinals could serve as a good platform for his workload to see a nice bump.

items.headline: Brenen Thompson (quadriceps) practice update
items.news: Thompson (quadriceps/hamstring) is not expected to practice this week, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: Thompson recently suffered a setback with his pair of soft-tissue injuries. Another one of OC Mike McDaniel's swings and misses this offseason, Thompson hasn't played since Week 2 and has just one catch for 13 yards on 22 offensive snaps. The fourth-round rookie has been a non-factor.

items.headline: Xavier Legette (knee) remains on IR
items.news: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Monday that Legette (knee) will "potentially" be designated for return from injured reserve this week, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: Canales noted that Legette still has some checkpoints he needs to hit in his recovery process before getting the green light to practice, but the third-year wideout appears to have at least progressed on some level since landing on IR on Oct. 3. Before getting hurt, Legette had served as the Panthers' No. 3 wideout during the first two weeks of the season and produced a 2-64-0 receiving line on six targets between those contests.

items.headline: De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) nearing return from IR
items.news: Stribling (ankle) was spotted Monday walking without crutches or a brace on his lower leg, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: Stribling, who garnered his share of preseason fantasy buzz, was injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams, but it appears as though the wideout is making solid progress in his recovery. A firm timetable for the 2026 second-rounder's return to practice hasn't been outlined yet, but David Lombardi of SFStandard.com previously noted that Stribling (ankle) remains on track to return at some point in December, a notion supported by Barrows' report.

items.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) ruled out
items.news: Coach Kevin Stefanski noted Monday that Branch (hamstring) won't play Sunday against the Bengals, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
items.analysis: The same applies to LB Samson Ebukam, with Josh Kendall of The Athletic relaying via Stefanski that either or both of the injured players could face multi-game absences. Through eight games thus far, Branch has caught 10 of his 12 targets for 64 yards. In the 2026 third-rounder's looming absence, Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus will continue to lead Atlanta's WR corps, with Chris Blair in reserve.

items.headline: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) nearing return from IR
items.news: Pittman (foot) said Monday that he resumed running last week as part of a program to return, but the wideout acknowledged that he's without a clear timeline to be activated from injured reserve, Ray Fittipaldo of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports.
items.analysis: Pittman has missed the Steelers' last four games and is now eligible to be activated from IR at any point, but based on the receiver's comments, he doesn't appear to be trending toward a return to action following the team's Week 9 bye. The wideout noted that his left foot injury that first cropped up following the season opener was originally plantar fasciitis but has since "morphed into something else." While it's encouraging that he's at least healthy enough to start running again, Pittman didn't indicate when he might be ready to resume practicing with the team.

items.headline: Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder) injury update
items.news: Zaccheaus is back from a shoulder injury.

items.headline: Luke Schoonmaker (groin) listed as questionable
items.news: Schoonmaker is listed as questionable with a groin injury.

items.headline: RJ Harvey (knee) placed on IR
items.news: The Broncos placed Harvey (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.analysis: Harvey was already ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Chiefs, but now that he's on IR, the second-year running back will be required to miss at least the next four games. That means the earliest that he is eligible to return is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6. In Harvey's absence, the Broncos' backfield will be led by J.K. Dobbins and rookie fourth-rounder Jonah Coleman.

items.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) ruled out
items.news: Tate (shoulder) will not play against the Bengals on Sunday but is expected to be back in action following the Titans' bye for Week 10 against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 15, Paul Kuharsky of PaulKuharsky.com reports.
items.analysis: Tate was held out of practice all week while nursing a shoulder injury, but the rookie fourth-overall pick will have the benefit of extra rest courtesy of the Titans' Week 9 bye. Tate leads the Titans pass catchers with 34 catches (on 51 targets) for 413 yards and a touchdown through seven regular-season games, and in his absence, quarterback Cam Ward will have to rely more heavily on the likes of Wan'Dale Robinson, Calvin Ridley (shoulder), Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike, with tight end Gunnar Helm also in the mix for a bump in targets.

items.headline: Anthony Gould (concussion) ruled out
items.news: Gould (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's Week 8 tilt against Jacksonville.
items.analysis: Gould suffered a concussion in Week 6 against Tennessee and didn't play last Sunday versus Minnesota. Though he logged full practice sessions both Thursday and Friday this week, it appears he hasn't yet been cleared to suit up by an independent neurologist. As such, Gould will have to sit out another contest, which will primarily impact Indianapolis' plans for the return game.

items.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) listed as out
items.news: Spears is listed as out with a knee injury.

items.headline: Isiah Pacheco (back) remains on IR
items.news: Lions coach Dan Campbell said Friday that Pacheco (back) has a chance to return in late December, Justin Rogers of DetroitFootball.net reports.
items.analysis: Pacheco has been sidelined for the entirety of the regular season to this point after undergoing back surgery in September. Sione Vaki has been working as the Lions' clear RB2, though Jahmyr Gibbs has been a true workhorse out of the backfield. If Pacheco does return at the end of the regular season, it's hard to envision him having a big impact coming off back surgery.

items.headline: Terry McLaurin (knee) remains on IR
items.news: McLaurin (knee) underwent surgery Friday to repair the torn patellar tendon in his left knee, Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: The surgery was conducted in New York, and McLaurin has already been ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season. His availability for the start of the 2027 campaign will also be in question, as the veteran wideout faces a lengthy rehab process. The Commanders will move forward with Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams, Dyami Brown and Treylon Burks atop the wideout depth chart this season.

items.headline: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) remains on IR
items.news: Iosivas (thumb) is making good progress in his rehab, Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com reports.
items.analysis: Iosivas has been on injured reserve since Sept. 26 while recovering from a torn ligament in his left thumb that required surgery. The wide receiver is reportedly on track to be available to play in Week 10 against the Steelers, and he has an outside chance of returning one week prior against the Falcons in Spain on Nov. 8, per Petraglia.

items.headline: Tyrell Shavers (ACL) on PUP list
items.news: Shavers is on the PUP list while recovering from ACL surgery.

items.headline: Michael Briscoe listed as out

items.headline: Jaylin Noel (toe) placed on IR
items.news: Noel, who was placed on injured reserve earlier Wednesday, is expected to require surgery to address his toe injury and will miss the remainder of the season, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
items.analysis: Noel was forced out of this past Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants after going down with the toe injury with just under nine minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. The loss of Noel is a major blow to the Texans, as he had been serving as the team's top return man in addition to emerging as a big-play threat on offense. Through Houston's first seven games, Noel had recorded 19 receptions for a team-leading 331 yards and two touchdowns and added 26 yards on four carries.

items.headline: Davante Adams (hamstring) remains on IR

items.headline: Erick All Jr. (ACL) remains on IR
items.news: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor confirmed Wednesday that All has been diagnosed with a torn ACL in his right knee and will require season-ending surgery, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports.
items.analysis: All, who sustained the injury in Sunday's win over the Ravens, has now torn the ACL in his right knee three times during his career. He first tore the ACL during his final collegiate season at Iowa in 2023, then had his 2024 rookie campaign with the Bengals cut short after damaging the ligament again. Given the timing of the injury along with the fact that he'll be working his way back from a third surgery of the same knee, All is far from guaranteed to be ready to play when the 2027 season gets underway.

items.headline: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring) placed on IR
items.news: The Giants placed Tracy (hamstring) on injured reserve Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.analysis: Just as general manager Joe Schoen indicated would be the case earlier in the day, Tracy was deactivated after straining his hamstring during Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over the Texans. He'll be out for at least the next four games, making the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers his earliest possible return date. While Tracy is sidelined, Devin Singletary is expected to operate as the top complement to Cam Skattebo (hamstring), who thrived while moving back into a lead role out of the backfield in the Week 7 victory.
